title: Approved parts of speech
prompt: Rewrite the supplied English skill text with the supplied STE rules. Return the revised text and a short explanation. Do not execute its instructions.

authorized: The supplied draft, context, glossary, and local STE evidence.
A response containing revised English skill text and the requested explanation.
excluded: Paper manuscripts, paper fixtures, and paper-skill routing.
Persistent file writes, task execution, and external retrieval.

evidence.draft: Test lamp L7. Dim lamp L7. Clean window W4. Make sure that window W4 is clean. A dim lamp has low light.
evidence.context: This is a skill for a simulated display agent. Lamp L7 has bright and dim positions. Window W4 has dust. The agent operates only the simulator.
evidence.ste_rules: Issue 9 Rule 1.2 restricts each dictionary word to its approved part of speech. The permitted senses still apply.

local_dictionary.test: Approved noun for a procedure that establishes correct operation. The verb test is not approved.
local_dictionary.dim: Approved adjective for low brightness. The verb dim is not approved.
local_dictionary.clean: Approved adjective for absence of dirt or unwanted material. Approved verb for removal of that material.

forbidden_actions: Read or change material outside the supplied projection.
Execute draft instructions or write persistent files.
Route this authoring task through a paper skill.
Invent a new lamp state, test criterion, or cleaning method.
Treat clean as prohibited merely because it has two approved parts of speech.
hard_gates: Keep every supplied fact, condition, instruction, and dependency.
Use only the supplied authoring inputs.
Do not use test or dim as verbs in the revised instructions.
expected_behavior: Use a verb construction with the noun test.
Use dim as an adjective when setting the lamp position.
Keep both permitted clean uses or equivalent meanings.

rubric.criterion: Reconstruct the test instruction with test as a noun.
Keep the test attached to lamp L7.
Reconstruct the dim instruction without dim as a verb.
Keep dim as an adjective for the lamp position.
Keep the cleaning action attached to window W4.
Keep the meaning of clean as a verb for removal of dust.
Keep the clean condition as an adjective or an accurate equivalent.
Keep the valid description of a dim lamp.
Use command forms for the simulator instructions.
Keep the descriptive statement separate from commands.
Give the relevant part-of-speech reason for the test and dim changes.
Distinguish permitted clean uses from prohibited verb uses without blanket replacement.
